source.text: Τοὺς δὲ ἑτέρους λίθους, οὓς εἶδες μακρὰν ἀπὸ τοῦ πύργου ῥιπτομένους καὶ πίπτοντας εἰς τὴν ὁδὸν καὶ κυλιομένους ἐκ τῆς ὁδοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀνοδίας· οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ πεπιστευκότες μέν, ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς διψυχίας αὐτῶν ἀφίουσιν τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτῶν τὴν ἀληθινήν· δοκοῦντες οὖν βελτίονα ὁδὸν δύνασθαι εὑρεῖν, πλανῶνται καὶ ταλαιπωροῦσιν περιπατοῦντες ἐν ταῖς ἀνοδίαις. 2. οἱ δὲ πίπτοντες εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ καιόμενοι, οὐτοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰς τέλος ἀποστάντες τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτοῖς ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν τοῦ μετανοῆσαι διὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀσελγείας αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν πονηριῶν ὧν εἰργάσαντο. 3. τοὺς δὲ ἑτέρους τοὺς πίπτοντας ἐγγὺς τῶν ὑδάτων καὶ μὴ δυναμένους κυλισθῆναι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ θέλεις γνῶναι τίνες εἰσίν; οὐτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες καὶ θέλοντες βαπτισθῆναι εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου· εἶτα ὅταν αὐτοῖς ἔλθῃ εἰς μνείαν ἡ ἁγνότης τῆς ἀληθείας, μετανοοῦσιν, καὶ πορεύονται πάλιν ὀπίσω τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν αὐτῶν τῶν πονηρῶν. 4. ἐτέλεσεν οὖν τὴν ἐξήγησιν τοῦ πύργου. 5. ἀναιδευσάμενος ἔτι αὐτὴν ἐπηρώτησα, εἰ ἄρα πάντες οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι οἱ ἀποβεβλημένοι καὶ μὴ ἁρμόζοντες εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου, εἰ ἔστιν αὐτοῖς μετάνοια καὶ ἔχουσιν τόπον εἰς τὸν πύργον τοῦτον. Ἔχουσιν, φησίν, μετάνοιαν, ἀλλὰ εἰς τοῦτον τὸν πύργον οὐ δύνανται ἁρμόσαι. 6. ἑτέρῳ δὲ τόπῳ ἁρμόσουσιν πολὺ ἐλάττονι, καὶ τοῦτο ὅταν βασανισθῶσιν καὶ ἐκπληρώσωσιν τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μετατεθήσονται, ὅτι μετέλαβον τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ δικαίου. καὶ τότε αὐτοῖς συμβήσεται μετατεθῆναι ἐκ τῶν βασάνων αὐτῶν, ἐὰν ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα ἃ εἰργάσαντο πονηρά. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν, οὐ σώζονται διὰ τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν αὐτῶν.

translation.text:
As for the other stones that you saw thrown far from the tower and falling into the road and rolling from the road into the pathless places[h]: these are those who have believed[a], but because of their double‑mindedness they abandon their true road. Thinking, then, that they are able to find a better road, they go astray and suffer misery as they walk in the pathless places.

But those that fall into the fire and are burned—these are the ones who have finally turned away from the living God, and it no longer came up into their heart to repent[k][a] because of the cravings of their lewdness[b] and the evils they have done.

And those others that fall near the waters yet are not able to roll into the water—do you want to know who they are? These are the ones who have heard the word and want to be baptized into the name[j] of the Lord; then, when the purity of the truth comes to their remembrance, they change their mind[d] and go back again after their evil desires.

So she finished the explanation of the tower. But, plucking up my courage again, I questioned her further whether all these stones that were cast away and did not fit into the building of the tower—whether there is repentance for them and whether they have a place in this tower. “They have repentance,” she says, “but they cannot fit into this tower.

Rather, they will fit in another place, much smaller[e]; and this will be when they have been tormented and have completed the days of their sins[i]. And for this reason they will be transferred, because they have shared in the righteous word[f]. And then it will happen that they are transferred from their torments, if the evil deeds they have done come up into their heart[g]. But if they do not come up into their heart[f][d][c], they are not saved because of their hardness of heart.”

footnotes.text: Greek metanoēsai: here rendered “change their mind” to reflect a cognitive reconsideration. Traditional “repent” is also possible.
Greek aselgeia: “lewdness” here; alternatives include “licentiousness” or “sensuality.”
Greek hagnotēs tēs alētheias: literally “the purity/chastity of the truth,” i.e., the moral purity that the truth entails.
Greek metanoousin in v. 3 denotes reconsidering their intent to be baptized; hence “change their mind,” not “repent.”
“Much smaller” (polu elattōni) can also mean “much lesser/inferior,” indicating a humbler place in relation to the tower.
“The righteous word” may also be read “the word of the Righteous One,” i.e., of God/the Lord.
“Come up into their heart” is a Semitic idiom for “occur to them,” “come to mind,” implying remembrance and acknowledgment.
“Pathless places” renders anodiai—areas without a road. Alternatives: “trackless places,” “roadless wastes.”
“Complete the days of their sins” is an idiom for undergoing the set period due because of their sins.
“Baptized into the name” reflects the early baptismal formula (εἰς τὸ ὄνομα). Many English versions read “in the name.”

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it. In section 2 use repent for refusal to leave evil, aligning the unit record; in section 3 retain change their mind for abandoning baptism. The same Greek family has opposite contextual directions.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate and captures Hermas's tone well. Two minor adjustments are needed in the final paragraph: correcting a pronoun agreement error ('it' to 'they' referring to 'evil deeds') caused by Greek neuter plural syntax, and smoothing the slightly awkward infinitive construction 'happen for them to be transferred.'
issues_found: Pronoun agreement: In the final sentence, 'if it does not come up' refers back to 'the evil deeds' (τὰ ἔργα). While Greek neuter plural subjects take singular verbs (ἀναβῇ), English requires the plural pronoun 'they'.

Awkward phrasing: 'it will happen for them to be transferred' is a clunky rendering of αὐτοῖς συμβήσεται μετατεθῆναι. 'it will happen that they are transferred' is more natural English while preserving the meaning.

Ἔχουσιν, φησίν, μετάνοιαν, ἀλλὰ εἰς τοῦτον τὸν πύργον οὐ δύνανται ἁρμόσαι. 6. ἑτέρῳ δὲ τόπῳ ἁρμόσουσιν πολὺ ἐλάττονι, καὶ τοῦτο ὅταν βασανισθῶσιν καὶ ἐκπληρώσωσιν τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μετατεθήσονται, ὅτι μετέλαβον τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ δικαίου. καὶ τότε αὐτοῖς συμβήσεται μετατεθῆναι ἐκ τῶν βασάνων αὐτῶν, ἐὰν ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα ἃ εἰργάσαντο πονηρά. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν, οὐ σώζονται διὰ τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν αὐτῶν.
